newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Belgium proposes compromise on EU budget pact.
newsitem.headline: Belgium proposes compromise on EU budget pact.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt on Thursday proposed a compromise on a pact to ensure fiscal discipline under the EU's planned monetary union and said there had been a fairly favourable response to it.
"I believe it is a bit of a tradition for Belgium to seek a compromise," he said.

"The response was fairly favourable," he told reporters during a pause in talks among European Union ministers aimed at settling a dispute over how rigid the rules should be in the proposed stability pact limiting budget deficits.

Maystadt said there was 95 percent agreement on the pact, but ministers had not yet resolved their main argument over how to define the special circumstances which would exempt countries from fines if they ran up big deficits.

He declined to say exactly what he was proposing but said it was based on the Maastricht treaty, the basis of the EU's plans for economic and monetary union (EMU). The treaty provided a basis for a judgement by EU ministers, he said.
"We have a basis which is the treaty. There is nothing about automaticity. It is the Council (ministers) which can decide on the basis of a global assessment," he said.
Automaticity means limiting political discretion to exempt countries from fines for exceeding the deficit ceiling.
Maystadt was speaking during a pause in talks between EU ministers aimed at resolving a dispute over the pact.
Maystadt said ministers were 95 percent agreed on the pact, but still had to work out how to define the exceptional circumstances which would exempt countries from fines.
The ministerial talks, taking place on the eve of a summit of EU leaders, were likely to drag on for some time.
But Maystadt said EU leaders would prefer the dispute on the stability pact to be settled by finance ministers rather than allowing the discussions to drag on into the summit.
"In my opinion the heads of state would prefer for it to be agreed between us," he said.
He said there were several delegations in favour of a fairly strict definition of the kind of circumstances which would justify an exemption from fines.
There were several options on the table in defining these exceptional circumstances, he said.
